Ubuntu is made by Canonical, so there's a lot under the hood that is exclusive to Ubuntu, which isn't found in Debian.

For instance, Canonical has created their own, proprietary init system (think Systemd or SysVInit) for Ubuntu, called UpStart. It works on Debian, but not well. It also isn't naturally supported in Debian as it is in Ubuntu. This means BIG changes in terms of how your systems boots and functions.

Also, Canonical is creating their own proprietary display manager, Mir, instead of putting support behind Wayland. This means even more differences in how your overall system is coded and runs.
